'''Eddie "E. J." Williams Jr.''' (born November 14, 2001)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Manie |date=September 25, 2019 |title=Clemson football recruit E.J. Williams was raised in football village |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/videos/sports/college/clemson/2019/09/25/clemson-football-eddie-williams-mother-recruiting/2437879001/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date= |title=E.J. Williams |url=https://clemsontigers.com/sports/football/roster/e-j-williams/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] |language=en-US}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]]. He was signed by the Raiders after going undrafted in the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Williams attended [[Central High School (Phenix City, Alabama)|Central High School]] in [[Phenix City, Alabama]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ankony |first=Jack |date=January 6, 2023 |title=Clemson Wide Receiver E.J. Williams Transfers to Indiana |url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/football/clemson-wide-receiver-ej-williams-transfers-to-indiana-football |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] }}</ref> During his junior and senior seasons there, he recorded 84 receptions for 1,407 yards and 19 touchdowns, including 44 receptions, 739 yards and 11 touchdowns in his senior season alone.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> He was selected to the [[Under Armour All-America Game]] after his senior year and was also named the Most Valuable Player from the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star game where he had 6 receptions for 98 yards.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He received 25 [[NCAA Division I]] offers, including from [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]], [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], but ultimately committed to [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=E.J. Williams Jr. Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/recruitment/ej-williams-113493/recruitinterests/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[247Sports]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rice |first=Jim |date=August 24, 2019 |title=Clemson football again lands Alabama's top wide receiver prospect |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2019/08/24/clemson-football-again-lands-alabamas-top-wide-receiver-prospect/2109597001/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] }}</ref>

==College career==

=== Clemson (2020–2022) ===

==== 2020 season ====
{{See also|2020 Clemson Tigers football team}}
In his freshman year, Williams played in 12 games, starting four, and recorded 24 receptions for 306 yards, both of which were fifth-highest on the team, along with 2 touchdowns.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Shanesy |first=Todd |date=January 1, 2021 |title=3 things to know about Clemson wide receiver E.J. Williams |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2021/01/01/ej-williams-clemson-football-wide-receiver-tigers-sugar-bowl-facts/4107442001/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] }}</ref> He caught his first touchdown on a 5-yard pass from [[Trevor Lawrence]] to go with 3 receptions for 38 yards receiving in a 52–17 win against [[2020 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|Pittsburgh]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Shanesy |first=Todd |date=November 28, 2020 |title=Clemson freshman E.J. Williams honors father with number change, first career touchdown |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2020/11/28/clemsons-e-j-williams-honors-late-father-scores-first-touchdown/6403771002/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Clemson 52-17 Pittsburgh (Nov 28, 2020) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game/_/gameId/401234651/pitt-clemson |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref> Before the game that took place on [[Military Appreciation Day]], Williams changed his jersey number from 6 to 39 to honor his father, Eddie, who was a [[sergeant first class]] in the U.S. Army; he died at the age of 39.<ref name=":7" /> Clemson went 10–2 for the season and advanced to the [[2020 ACC Championship Game]], where they defeated [[2020 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]] 34–10. Williams had a career-high 80 yards off 4 receptions in that game; he scored his second touchdown of the season off a 33-yard pass from Lawrence.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Raynor |first=Grace |date=December 24, 2020 |title=How Clemson WR E.J. Williams is grabbing his chance and wowing with it |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2280966/2020/12/24/clemson-e-j-williams-wide-recevers/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |work=[[The Athletic]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The team played against [[2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]] in the [[2021 Sugar Bowl|Sugar Bowl]] where they lost 49–28; Williams caught 5 passes for 45 yards.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ohio State 49-28 Clemson (Jan 1, 2021) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game/_/gameId/401240173/ohio-state-clemson |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2021 season ====
{{See also|2021 Clemson Tigers football team}}
In Clemson's first game of the season against Georgia, Williams sustained a thumb injury in the 10–3 loss and was initially expected to miss 4–5 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2021 |title=Clemson WR Williams will miss 4-to-5 weeks with thumb injury |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-college-football-clemson-tigers-football-ff44491c7a5df8619de99238d058979e |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Georgia 10-3 Clemson (Sep 4, 2021) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game/_/gameId/401281946/georgia-clemson |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref> However, Williams decided to postpone surgery on it and was cleared to play shortly afterward.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=September 7, 2021 |title=Clemson wide receiver E.J. Williams will try to play despite injured thumb |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2021/09/07/clemson-football-wide-receiver-ej-williams-try-play-through-injured-thumb-injury/5763332001/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2021 |title=Dabo: Clemson WR Williams good to go |url=https://www.wspa.com/sports/clemson-tigers-sports/clemson-wr-williams-will-miss-4-to-5-weeks-with-thumb-injury/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[WSPA-TV]] |place=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Gavin |date=September 8, 2021 |title=Swinney updates Williams injury |url=https://www.theclemsoninsider.com/2021/09/08/swinney-updates-williams-injury/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=The Clemson Insider |language=en}}</ref> Williams caught 9 passes for 66 yards in his sophomore season while playing in eight games, starting two of them; he also made a tackle on special teams against [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]].<ref name=":1" /> Head coach [[Dabo Swinney]] ruled Williams out for the [[2021 Cheez-It Bowl|Cheez-It Bowl]] against [[2021 Iowa State Cyclones football team|Iowa State]] after he contracted [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lentz |first=Zach |date=December 28, 2021 |title=COVID Hits Clemson |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/covid-19-hits-the-clemson-tigers |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=December 28, 2021 |title=Clemson's depleted receiver corps takes another hit with E.J. Williams out for Cheez-It Bowl |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2021/12/28/clemson-football-ej-williams-covid-protocol-out-cheez-it-bowl/9033249002/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== 2022 season ====
{{See also|2022 Clemson Tigers football team}}
Williams missed spring practice prior to the 2022 season with a knee injury that he first sustained in 2021 and underwent an [[Knee arthroscopy|arthroscopy]] as a result.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shanesy |first=Todd |date=March 4, 2022 |title=Clemson injuries: 'Recurring issues' forced knee surgery for wide receiver E.J. Williams |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2022/03/04/clemson-football-injury-news-updates-surgery-ej-williams-wide-receiver-dabo-swinney/9367767002/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Niziolek |first=Michael |date=July 29, 2024 |title=Can Indiana football receiver E.J. Williams overcome his ‘biggest nemesis’ this fall? |url=https://www.heraldtimesonline.com/story/sports/college/iu/2024/07/29/indiana-football-2024-season-ej-williams-wide-receivers-curt-cignetti-clemson-injuries/74583973007/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The Herald-Times]] }}</ref> He totaled 7 receptions for 70 yards in 242 offensive snaps as Clemson went 11–3 for the season.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Senkiw |first=Brad |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Ups and Downs: Clemson Closes Out 2022 With Struggles Against Tennessee |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/ups-and-downs-clemson-closes-out-2022-with-struggles-against-tennessee |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] }}</ref>

=== Indiana (2023–present) ===

==== 2023 season ====
{{See also|2023 Indiana Hoosiers football team}}

Williams Jr. |url=https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/football/roster/e-j-williams-jr-/20035 |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]]}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Illinois 48-45 Indiana (Nov 11, 2023) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game/_/gameId/401520383/indiana-illinois |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref> Despite this, Indiana was defeated by a score of 48–45 in overtime.<ref name=":2" />

{{See also|2024 Indiana Hoosiers football team}}Williams sustained a hamstring injury prior to the season during fall camp practice.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Jared |date=April 8, 2024 |title=WR EJ Williams has one last chance to reach potential at IU — and both sides need each other more than ever |url=https://247sports.com/college/indiana/article/wr-ej-williams-has-one-last-chance-to-reach-potential-at-iu-and-both-sides-need-each-other-more-than-ever-248449550/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[247Sports]] |language=en}}</ref> He played in Indiana's Week 4 game against [[2024 Charlotte 49ers football team|Charlotte]], but did not have a reception.<ref name=":4" /> He had a 37-yard reception from [[Kurtis Rourke]] against [[2024 Northwestern Wildcats football team|Northwestern]] and a 12-yard catch against [[2024 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team|Nebraska]].<ref name=":4" /> In October, Williams entered the transfer portal, stating "I made this decision because the team was perfectly fine without me in the game and I also want to have a chance at being able to continue my career at the professional level."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ankony |first=Jack |date=October 21, 2024 |title=Wide Receiver E.J. == Personal life ==
Williams was born to Eddie and Vontrelle Williams, both of whom served in the military.<ref name=":3" /> His father was a U.S. Army veteran who held the title of [[sergeant first class]]. He died at the age of 39, when Williams was 8 years old.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Sentell |first=Jeff |date=January 21, 2019 |title=Dream school? Junior receiver E.J. Williams just had a big unofficial visit to UGA |url=https://www.dawgnation.com/football/recruiting/junior-wr-e-j-williams-just-spent-a-big-first-unofficial-visit-at-uga/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=DawgNation |language=English}}</ref> He stated that his father influenced him into playing football, stating "He loved the game a lot. Every time I came home from school he was on the couch just getting home from work watching football and he really got me into the game at a young age."<ref name=":5" /> His older sister, Kahlia Lawrence, played college basketball for the [[Mercer Bears women's basketball|Mercer Bears]] and was selected 24th overall in the [[2018 WNBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Lynx]]; she is currently a graduate assistant for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane women's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane women's basketball team]].<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kahlia Lawrence |url=https://tulsahurricane.com/sports/womens-basketball/roster/coaches/kahlia-lawrence/1958 |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[Tulsa Golden Hurricanes]] |language=en}}</ref> Williams and Lawrence were classmates when they previously lived in [[El Paso, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shanesy |first=Todd |date=December 3, 2020 |title=Clemson freshman E.J. Williams had movie-script game in honoring his late father |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2020/12/03/clemson-freshman-has-movie-script-game-honoring-his-late-father/6471306002/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> However, after their father's death, the family moved to [[Columbus, Georgia]] where Williams began his football career later at Clemson.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=May 15, 2020 |title=Football Freshman Focus: EJ Williams |url=https://clemsonsportsnews.com/football-freshman-focus-ej-williams/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=Clemson Sports News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Williams and his father were [[Georgia Bulldogs football]] fans growing up.<ref name=":5" /> He idolized NFL running back [[Todd Gurley]] and wide receiver [[A. J. Green]].<ref name=":5" /> He is close friends with [[Justyn Ross]], a two-time Super Bowl champion with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] who was a teammate in Central High School and Clemson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Connolly |first=Matt |date=December 27, 2020 |title=Justyn Ross starred as a freshman in playoff. This Clemson receiver could do the same |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article248102145.html |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]}}</ref>
